items.statement: Gross margin at 31.5% in Q2 FY26, below 32-34% guidance range due to inventory and fixed costs
items.quote: So Rachna, my gross margin is at 31.5% okay . Typically, we have given a guidance of about 32% to 34%. And last 4 quarters, we've been at about 32%, 32.5%. This 1 quarter is a blip, largely inventories, fixed cost of factories, all that. We remain in that guidance of 32% to 34%

items.statement: Festive season buildup and improving retail sentiment expected to drive stronger H2 demand
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the second half of the year. The festive season buildup, coupled with improving retail sentiment and normalization of channel inven tory across the industry is expected to drive stronger demand momentum

items.statement: BEE star ratcheting for ceiling fans effective January 1, 2026 expected to accelerate premium energy-efficient adoption
items.quote: With regulatory developments like BEE Star ratcheting for fans effective 1st January 2026 , premium and energy -efficient categories are poised for accelerated adoption in the years to come.

items.statement: Industry price hike of 3-4% expected from star ratcheting, commodity dependent
items.quote: On the last question on your ratcheting -led pricing, if I were to normalize and keep the commodity pricing constant, I think the price hike that the industry should look at should be about 3% to 4%, okay . Unlike the first time when non -star to star rated happened, the price increase was huge. This time, it should be about 3% to 4%, but it all depends on how the commodity and if LME continues to

items.statement: Took 1.5% average price increase in fans in September to cushion commodity rise
items.quote: Given the softness, I wish we could have taken a price increase much earlier in the quarter. But towards the end in September, we did take a price increase in fans. It was in the tune of on average about 1.5% averaged out f or the category, fans. So it did give a little bit of cushion against the commodity rise.

items.statement: Strong professional lighting pipeline with rising project inquiries and new authority onboarding
items.quote: On the professional lighting front, we recorded double -digit growth, fuelled by successful execution of key projects in street lighting and facade segments. A strong pipeline, coupled with rising project inquiries and onboarding of new authorities, position us well for sustained growth in the coming quarters.

items.statement: New product developments contributed almost one-third of fans revenue this quarter
items.quote: Our innovation-led growth is underscored by our new product developments, which contributed almost one third of our fans revenues this quarter.

items.statement: Transitioned Pune market from master distributor to direct-to-market model
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully transitioned the Pune market from master distributor to direct to market. With this, our DTM footprint continues to expand rapidly in expanding markets, reinforcing our commitment to deeper market penetration and agile distribution.

items.statement: Added Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh to direct service network for faster response times
items.quote: Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh were added to our direct service network, enhancing customer experience through faster response times and more efficient last mile service delivery.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility commissioned with state-of-the-art TPW production capability for South markets
items.quote: Hyderabad is a facility which is state -of-the-art. Unfortunately, there's been a very soft season, but our facility to produce TPW of a high quality is there. And given the fact that in Hyderabad, o ur speed, agility to service the market, our logistic cost when -- hopefully, for the next season would be much sharper, much better.

items.statement: Working capital increased to 32 days due to cooling category inventory buildup; expects normalization in next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, it should. There's been a little bit of inventory buildup, which look at, I spoke about cooling categories. Typically, we don't carry this kind of inventory for TPW around this time. We don't carry coolers inventory around this time. Even for ceiling fans, it has been slightly higher than what we would have ideally anticipated over here. In the next two quarters, we should be able to normaliz

items.statement: Fan market share gained 60 basis points YTD across MD and DTM markets despite soft summer
items.quote: On a YTD basis, if we were to look at it, we've gained our market share by 60 basis points. Both our MD markets and the DTM markets have gained market share. There have been some opportunities in some of the markets. Those will always remain. But by and large, we've gained market share across the country.

items.statement: Consumer lighting market share gained 70-80 basis points for seventh consecutive quarter
items.quote: On the lighting, especially in the consumer lighting, we've gained market share continuously now for the seventh quarter. Our market shares have moved up by almost 70-80 basis points. It's still a long way for us.

items.statement: Lighting B2B/B2C split at 75-25, aspiring to reach industry leader 60-40 balance
items.quote: The second question you asked was on the lighting split between -- so we still have a large dependency on the CLUM side. We are typically around 75 -25. Hopefully, we should look at some of the leaders in the industry who sit at about 60-40. While we are gaining our momentum on the B2B side of the lighting, we want both to grow.

items.statement: DTM transition time reduced to 45-60 days from initial longer periods
items.quote: And yes, transition time when we started was very huge. We now feel that on a good this thing, it could be a 45 to 60 days that we can do a transition.

items.statement: Cooler segment saw 80% decline in Q2; TPW inventory higher than ideal due to soft summer
items.quote: Cooler segment has seen about a minus 80% for us, and I'm sure the industry is going to be like that only. On the last question on your ratcheting -led pricing, if I were to normalize and keep the commodity pricing constant, I think the price hike that the industry should look at should be about 3% to 4%, okay . Unlike the first time when non -star to star rated happened, the price increase was hu

items.statement: E-commerce channel delivered high double-digit growth led by appliances and quick commerce participation
items.quote: Our refreshed range and improved channel visibility in the e-com helped us capture early festive momentum, resulting in a high double -digit growth in the e-comm channel. Appliances led the surge supported by strong traction in emerging categories such as i rons, which gained incremental momentum. Meanwhile, our core categories like water heaters continue to deliver consistent growth in the e -com

items.statement: EBITDA rose 6.4% YoY to INR38 crores with 5.4% margin; PAT up 15.5% to INR12 crores
items.quote: Our EBITDA rose 6.4% year -on-year to INR38 crores with an EBITDA margin of 5.4%. Our profits after taxes were up by 15.5% year-on-year to INR12 crores.

items.statement: Lighting and switchgear segment grew 18.6% YoY; wires more than doubled on lower base
items.quote: Our lighting, switchgear and wires portfolio delivered strong quarterly revenue, registering a robust 18.6% year-on-year growth, underscoring the success of our strategy. Both switchgears and wires achieved robust growth, while wires more than doubling year-on-year, however, on a lower base.

items.statement: DTM markets showed resilience with single-digit growth despite seasonal headwinds in fans
items.quote: Despite seasonal headwinds in the fans category, DTM -led markets demonstrated resilience, registering single-digit growth and validating the long -term potential of the model.

items.statement: Launched Samvad program for all employees to listen to consumer calls and feedback
items.quote: We've started a program called Samvad, which is where all of us listen to consumer calls, consumer feedback and pick nuances, which we can then take back, change our process, change our products. So we're keeping that approach.

items.statement: LME commodity prices inching up; festive season typically sees commodity price increases
items.quote: On the commodity pricing, yes, you're right. The LME has gone up. But typically, around this time, festive time, the commodity prices go up. We are very hopeful that it softens -- our whole philosophy is that if it doesn't come down, at some point, we will pass on to the consumers.

items.statement: Project Sanchay contributed INR24 crores cost savings in H1 FY26
items.quote: Operationally, Project San chay remained central to our efficiency agenda and has contributed meaningfully to cost savings of INR24 crores in H1.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for H2 FY26 at 14-16% for core B2B business excluding consumer and institutional verticals
items.quote: We have said that for the balance year in terms of the EBITDA margins, we have guided that it will remain at the similar levels as the H1. In spite of pressures are rising and all, we are still hopeful that we will be able to push through this year with similar kind of margins and excluding the consumer and institutional business, we said we will be in the range of 14% - 16%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenues grew 18% YoY driven by healthy volume expansion across all three core businesses
items.quote: We are pleased to share that our revenues for Q2 FY26 grew by 18 % YoY, driven by healthy volume expansion across all three of our core businesses.

items.statement: HPPC, TSC, and AHN divisions grew 16%, 21%, and 29% YoY respectively in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Q2 FY26 reflected a strong growth trajectory across our four verticals with HPPC, TSC, , and AHN divisions growing 16%, 21%, and 29% YoY respectively.

items.statement: Exports rose 36% YoY in Q2 and 27% in H1, now contributing nearly 28% of overall revenues
items.quote: On the export front, our international business delivered robust growth with exports rising 36% YoY in Q2 and 27% in H1. This growth was driven by improved traction with key customers, higher wallet share with strategic partners, and deeper penetration in both existing and new geographies. We now derived nearly 28% of our overall revenues from exports, highlighting the expanding scale of our inter

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 12.3% in Q2 FY26 vs 13.2% last year; core EBITDA steady at around 15% excluding institutional and B2C verticals
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 71.9 crore with a margin of 12.3% compared to 13.2% in Q2 last year. Excluding the institutional and B2C verticals, our core EBITDA remained steady at around 15%.

items.statement: Total planned capital outlay of Rs. 192 crore; remaining projects to be commissioned and capitalized over next few months
items.quote: On the capex front, we have made significant progress with successful commissioning of our new capacities during the quarter. These additions take us closer to our total planned capital outlay of Rs. 192 crore, with the remaining projects to be commissioned and capitalized over the next few months.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex outflow of Rs. 142 crore; additional Rs. 20-25 crore expected in H2
items.value: Rs. 142 crore H1, Rs. 20-25 crore H2
items.quote: In terms of numbers, the first half saw an outflow of about Rs. 142 crore for capex. This number is not going to go up drastically, maybe another Rs. 5 crore – Rs. 10 crore more? Ketan Sablok: Yes, it should go up by another Rs. 20 crore – Rs. 25 crore, not more than that.

items.statement: Commissioned additional 20,000 MTPA at Dahej and 15,000 MTPA ethoxylation capacity at Unitop; second phase and other additions progressing for coming quarters
items.quote: On the manufacturing front, we are pleased to announce the successful commissioning of an additional 20,000 metric tons per annum capacity at our Dahej facility and 15,000 metric tons per annum of ethoxylation capacity at Unitop, marking the first phase of the planned 30,000 metric tons per annum expansion. The second phase and other capacity additions are progressing well and are expected to be c

items.statement: New Dahej plant scale-up over 2-3 years, peak utilization expected by FY28
items.quote: This plant has got capitalized in this quarter. The scale- up is going to happen over the next 2-3 years and our assessment is that by FY28, we should be reaching the peak utilization of this capex.

items.statement: Ethoxylation facilities running at optimal utilization 24/7; non-ethoxylation capacity mostly blending with flexibility
items.quote: Ethoxylation, we have about 30,000 tons at Unitop Dahej, which is practically running to the full production capacity, which is possible. We are utilizing the assets like 24/7, 365 days. And in fact, even in Diwali this time, we are running the assets because this month there is an EO shortage because the Dahej plant of Reliance is not operational.

items.statement: End of FY26 capacity expected at approximately 385,000 tons
items.quote: At the end of FY26, we will have a capacity of about 385,000 tons, approximately? Ketan Sablok: Yes, approximately.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from customers since September; resistance to price reductions but uncertainty on tariffs creating headwinds
items.quote: September onwards we faced a lot of resistance from the customers in terms of the pricing. This year I think, at least now it's a little difficult for us to really predict how the year is going to end up, but if we can maintain these kinds of margins for this year I think we would be quite happy.

items.statement: Developed new non-EO products including biosurfactants (target 250+ tons/year), CAPB, CDEA, silicon block polymers, silicon surfactant, esters, spin finish products, NMMO (150 to 300 tons), PEG cold powder, animal health fatty acids, vitami
items.quote: Over the past six to nine months, our teams have developed new products, both in Ethylene Oxide-based and non- EO-based, guided by green chemistry principles to deliver sustainable, scalable, and customized solutions for customers across industries. These developments strengthen our technology pipeline and enhance our ability to address emerging global trends and export opportunities in advanced c

items.statement: New ethoxylation reactors fungible for non-EO production; 50 products in pipeline for new facility
items.quote: We will be using the facilities for manufacturing non-Ethylene Oxide products or non-EO products. We are working in the R&D with a range of products for non-Ethoxylate which includes esters and emulsifiers. There are also many enzyme formulations, biocides, and disinfectants. We will be ramping up these products. A whole lot of about 50 products are in pipeline for us to start manufacturing there.

items.statement: Export growth driven by improved traction with key customers, higher wallet share with strategic partners, and deeper penetration in existing and new geographies
items.quote: This growth was driven by improved traction with key customers, higher wallet share with strategic partners, and deeper penetration in both existing and new geographies.

items.statement: US tariffs creating uncertainty; customers in agro, textile, home care exporting to US facing order delays and price pressure
items.quote: Many of these customers who we were supplying in the agro- industry they were exporting their Agro-formulations, the pesticide, pesticide, herbicide formulations to US and now that is under tariff but also, there are a lot of products which are not under tariff but our US customers are not willing to import, not willing, even orders which have been given are not being lifted. They say, we are not

items.statement: US tariffs on textile exports (50%) and agrochemicals creating headwinds for textile chemicals business; suppliers sharing risk case-by-case
items.quote: As you know, because of the tariffs on textile exports to the US, a lot of home textiles and terry towel companies are under pressure, as well as a lot of garment manufacturers which exports to the US are under pressure because of the 50% tariff. So, I believe that although this quarter textile chemicals did pretty well, there was a 10% growth QoQ, but we believe that there will be headwinds becau

items.statement: Net working capital increased to 102 days from 95 days in March; receivables stretched due to tight conditions and long payment cycle on major institutional sale
items.quote: The net working capital was higher during this quarter, where we ended at 102 days compared to 95 days in March. Given the slightly tight business conditions, some of the receivables have got stretched, and also a major institutional sale which we did in Q2 has a long payment cycle.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative in H1 due to working capital stretch; expected to turn positive by year-end as agro season tapers off
items.quote: No. This quarter, we had, as I already talked about, a little stretch on the working capital. I think that led to this negative cash flow. Hopefully, things will ease out in the coming 2 quarters and we should be back to the positive number by the end of the year.

items.statement: Board approved up to USD 8 million investment in Saudi Arabia subsidiary for feasibility studies and expansion evaluation; funding to be spaced out in tranches
items.quote: To support this initiative, our board has approved an investment of up to USD 8 million in Ros sari International Limited Company, our wholly owned subsidiary in Saudi Arabia. The proposed investment will be made in tranches and is intended to evaluate and expansion plans which align with the company's strategy to enhance its global presence and strengthen its position in international markets.

items.statement: Thailand blending unit capex small, coming on stream by end of Q3 FY26; may expand if successful
items.quote: The current investments in Southeast Asia or Thailand that we have done, that will also come on stream by the end of Q3. That is a small capex. It is not a very large payout because that is just a blending unit that we are setting up there. We will see how that pans out and then if required, we will set up a little more expanded facilities there.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty killing demand visibility; US customers not lifting orders even without tariffs due to daily policy uncertainty
items.quote: This uncertainty is killing. Similarly, we had a lot of textile chemical formulators who were buying our Ethoxylate and who were supplying to the textile industry and these have come into trouble. There were home and personal care customers who were making formulations for Walmart and Cosco and CVC. There are a lot many customers who are exporting to US and now everything is under cloud.

items.statement: Institutional and B2C business grew 1% YoY and 7% QoQ; losses reduced due to profitability and operational efficiency efforts
items.quote: Our institutional and B2C business remained soft during the quarter, growing around 1% YoY and 7% quarter-on-quarter. However, it is encouraging that losses in these verticals have reduced, driven by our efforts to improve profitability and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Buzil-Rossari revenue growth muted at 1.4% due to deliberate restriction of low-margin products to improve margins
items.quote: We have been restricting low margin products and trying to filter out some kind of range. The focus for the team was given is trying to improve margins in this, and that was the reason why we did not focus on the growth there. But growth will certainly come there.

items.statement: Iran sanctions impact minimal; methanol and acetic acid price spikes temporary, not substantial raw materials for company
items.quote: I think the major imports from Iran, one of the big ones was methanol. And methanol saw a spurt of Rs. 8 or Rs. 10 on the same day when this news came in. But methanol is not a very big raw material. Our consumption of methanol is very small. Acetic acid also was there, but acetic acid as a percentage of imports into India from Iran of the total imports was very negligible. It is not very big.

items.statement: KFC expansion pace expected at 60-80 stores per year
items.quote: Our current pace of expansion should be in the region of 60 to 80 stores a year.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store additions paused until brand revival and payback improvement
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, yes, there has been a struggle. So, we work on a calendar year. Last calendar year, we opened 20 odd stores. This year, we are so far negative 1. And yes, unless we see a revival in the brand growth in terms of SSSG and growth coming back, we do not see any meaningful additions to the count.

items.statement: Added 19 KFC, 2 Pizza Hut in India, 1 Pizza Hut and 1 Taco Bell in Sri Lanka in Q2 FY26
items.value: 19 KFC, 2 Pizza Hut, 1 Pizza Hut SL, 1 Taco Bell SL
items.quote: In Quarter 2, we added 19 KFC restaurants, 2 Pizza Huts in India, 1 Pizza Hut and 1 Taco Bell in Sri Lanka.

items.statement: Total restaurant count reached 997 as of 30th September; 1000th restaurant inaugurated at Gummidipoondi
items.quote: Our total restaurant count of 997 as on 30th September and with immense pride, we inaugurated the 1000th Sapphire restaurant yesterday at Gum midipoondi in Tamil Nadu and this is a KFC restaurant.

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA declined 12% YoY, margin at 11.3% down 240 bps
items.quote: Our consolidated restaurant EBITDA declined by 12% year -on-year. Margin was 11.3%, down 240 basis points.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin at 13.8%, impacted by negative SSSG, higher delivery mix, lower gross margin
items.quote: The restaurant EBITDA came at 13.8%, which was impacted by the negative SSSG on account of that Navratri impact, the higher delivery mix and lower gross margin.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA at 1.8%, breakeven excluding additional marketing investments
items.quote: Restaurant EBITDA came at 1.8%. If I exclude the additional marketing investments, which is over and above the Yum! agreements, the brand is at a breakeven level.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA improved to 15.4% from 12.7% in Q1 after mitigating minimum wage impact
items.quote: Restaurant EBITDA came in at 15.4% and if you guys would remember, Quarter 1 it was 12.7% and it was impacted by —as Sanjay mentioned —the minimum wage increase which came in somewhere in May but retrospectively from April, which we were not able to mitigate during the previous quarter but we were confident that we should be able to mitigate and that is reflected in our performance which came at r

items.statement: KFC gross margin dropped 110 bps YoY due to continued investment in 'Epic Saver' value offers
items.quote: Gross margin while it dropped 110 bps vis -a-vis last year. This is in similar line as Quarter 1 . The reason we dropped on gross margin vis-a-vis last year was as mentioned previously as well, that we continue to invest behind the value offers, namely the ' Epic Saver ' campaign.

items.statement: Pizza Hut gross margin stable at 74.4% QoQ, but invested 150-170 bps in H1 on value offers
items.quote: margin came at 74.4%, which is similar to Quarter 1. And as the case was in KFC, here too, we continue to invest significantly behind the value offers to try and drive the transactions

items.statement: Sri Lanka took 4-5% price increase in Q2 and reduced promotional offers, improving gross margin by 220 bps
items.quote: First, we took a 4 %-5% price increase in Quarter 2 . Also, there was some reduction in our promotional offers which helped us improve our margins by 220 bps.

items.statement: GST cut benefit of 0.5% on input prices passed on to consumers via 5-10% price reduction on top 7-10% selling lines from 22nd September
items.quote: Yes, from our input prices, there is a very small or marginal benefit, which we see 0.5% or less. And that we have pass ed on to the customers, although we would not have received the benefit immediately because we carry inventories. But yet, in good faith, we have passed on to the customers for both KFC and Pizza Hut.

items.statement: KFC SSSG -3% for quarter but flat ex-Navratri with positive transaction growth; extended 'Epic Saver' campaign to Q3 with 3 hero products
items.quote: While KFC was (3%) SSSG for the quarter, up to Navratri we were flat on SSSG, but positive on transaction. Therefore, we have extended this campaign to Quarter 3 also but included our 3 hero innovation products of Chizza, Double Down and the Gold Burger.

items.statement: Pizza Hut revenue declined 6% but Tamil Nadu grew double digits proving dine-in forward omni-channel strategy works
items.quote: Pizza Hut revenue declined by 6%. However, importantly in Tamil Nadu, which is a Sapphire exclusive territory, we grew double digit revenue. I think it just proves the Pizza Hut , Sapphire strategy and offers a clear hypothesis for why this brand can grow or why and how this brand can grow.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG 14% and revenue growth 18% in LKR terms (23% in INR), driven by brand innovation and value investment
items.quote: The SSSG came at 14% in LKR terms and while overall revenue grew at 18% in LKR terms. When converted to Indian rupees, the revenue grew at 23%.

items.statement: Q3 showing signs of recovery in first 16-17 days but overlapping Navratri; clearer view by end of November
items.quote: In Q3 , we are seeing signs of recovery and really it is 16 -17 days. And we are overlapping Navratri. So, the numbers look very good at this moment , Avi. But I will just let a little more time go. Perhaps at the end of November, we could say that things have started to improve.

items.statement: KFC rolled out digital kiosks across 50% of estate; own delivery via KFC app is best performing channel
items.quote: We rolled out digital kiosks across 50% of our estate and our own delivery through the KFC app continues to be the best performing channel.

items.statement: Pizza Hut launched Ultimate Cheese Pizza, Cheesy Pocket, Cold Coffee range (80% stores); dine-in value offers: Buy 1 Get 3, 4-course meals @99, Unlimited Pizza Fridays
items.quote: And in this quarter, in October, we have launched the Ultimate Cheese Pizza and the Cheesy Pocket, which emphasizes or which looks at satisfying the customer need for additional cheese. It's a great product and I invite all of you all to try it. We have also launched the Cold Coffee range and it's in about 80% of our stores now.

items.statement: Pizza Hut dine-in contribution improved vs last year; dine-in SSSG better than delivery due to exclusive value offers
items.quote: Apart from innovation, we also focused on dine -in value. And you will see in Pizza Hut, our dine-in contribution actually improved versus last year. Exclusive value offerings like Buy 1 Get 3, 4 course meals starting @99 and Unlimited Pizza Fridays helped ensure that dine -in SSSG was better than delivery.

items.statement: KFC own app channel grew 2-3x faster than aggregators; late-night hours extended (some stores to 5 AM) driving delivery mix
items.quote: The first one, our O LO, which is our own channel, our own app performance has been really good over the last 1 year. It has grown probably 2X to 3X more than what aggregators would have delivered in terms of the growth, our own app.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Tamil Nadu mid-teens delta in SSSG, SSTG and revenue growth vs rest of country due to mass media advertising by both Sapphire and Yum!
items.quote: And finally, in Tamil Nadu, both Sapphire and Yum! continue to invest in mass media advertising. And we saw a mid-teens delta in performance between compared to the rest of the country, both SSSG as well as SG.

items.statement: Consumer discretionary spends constrained for 2 years; increased competition in food space compounding QSR growth challenges
items.quote: So, in general, and this has been consistent with what we have said up till now, we are finding that consumer discretionary spend s have been constrained. And that has been compounded further by a large number of competitors, generally in food. Now, this has been the case over the last, I would say 2 years. Nothing has improved from that perspective.

items.statement: GST reduction and income tax cuts expected to improve consumer sentiment and discretionary spending from Q3 and CY2026
items.quote: Along with all the work that we are doing, the macro trends also seem positive. GST reduction should put further money into consumer wallets as indeed has the income tax reduction. So, we are hoping that as we get into the Quarter 3 and into calendar year 2026, we should see consumer sentiment improving.

items.statement: Nominee director Rohitt Mutthoo resigned from board after leaving TR Capital (promoter shareholder entity)
items.quote: The resignation, Mr. Rohitt Mutthoo has left TR Capital and therefore, being a nominee director backed by TR Capital; therefore, he has to move out of the board of Sapphire Foods also. So, he has resigned from TR Capital. And therefore, he has to resign from all his obligations that he used to fulfill for TR Capital.

items.statement: KFC SSTG positive low single digit in Q1 and Q2 ex-Navratri despite flat/negative SSSG
items.quote: However, the SS TG was positive in Quarter 1 as well, low single digit. Quarter 2, while it is (3), because of the Navratri impact, ex-Navratri SSSG is flattish. And SSTG continues to remain again positive low single digit.

items.statement: KFC Q3 SSSG starting base ~+2.5% on festive quarter (vs +3% on Q2 base) due to Navratri shift
items.quote: Largely yes, except for a small difference that a 3% on a Quarter 2 base is a smaller base, that same 3% on a Diwali and a festive quarter could be 2.5 rather than 3 . That is the only small change. But yes, one should assume that we are probably starting 2.5% positive as we get into a Quarter 3.

items.statement: Pizza Hut expansion on hold until brand revival; new store paybacks not achieved at current breakeven level
items.quote: If the brand is overall in negative or just about breakeven, of course, the new stores would not be giving the desired paybacks. And at Sapphire, we have always called out that . Finally, our expansion would be guided by the strike rates and the paybacks we get on the new store's performance.

items.statement: Sri Lanka minimum wage increase of 27% in Q1 ate into EBITDA gains from 14% SSSG; impact may persist until cost annualizes
items.quote: And the drop happened because there was almost a 27% increase in minimum wages in Sri Lanka. It happened in May, effective from April, and it left us with a very small amount of time to try and mitigate that impact in Q uarter 1.

items.statement: Management expects full-year FY26 revenue to more than double H1 revenue but declines to give a fixed number due to commodity price volatility
items.quote: So typically, we should be more than doubling up what the revenue we have posted. But I would not like to give any kind of fixed number purely because it's a commodity.

items.statement: Management expects average EBITDA margin of 12-13% on a per-ton basis
items.quote: But yes, what I have explained to you is more or less that you can expect around 12% to 13% on an average EBITDA.

items.statement: Unit 2 in Surat with 140 metric tons per day processing capacity commissioned and ramped up; operated at full capacity for 3.5 months in H1 FY26
items.quote: The highlight of the year has been successful commissioning and ramp-up of our unit 2 in Surat with a processing capacity of 140 metric tons per day.

items.statement: Unit 3 land acquired at Vasaravi, Surat spanning 412,164 sq ft; will integrate renewable energy and expand by-product processing
items.quote: In addition, we have acquired industrial land for unit 3 at Vasaravi, Surat, Gujarat spanning 412,164 square feet which will be the cornerstone of our next phase of growth.

items.statement: Phase 1 capex completed in May; Phase 2 (CNSL oil processing) construction expected to complete by end FY26 or within a month in FY27; 4 MW solar plant orders placed with similar timeline
items.quote: We have now embarked upon the Phase 2, which is the CNSL stuff. As I have already mentioned previously that we may complete that before end of the year, FY '26 or maximum in a month in FY '27. We have also placed orders for the solar plants, which is around 4 megawatt capacity.

items.statement: H1 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 8.86%; consolidated EBITDA margin 8.78%; Q1 FY26 EBITDA negative, Q2 FY26 EBITDA positive and higher than H1 total
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 8.86% demonstrating improved operating leverage and cost efficiency.

items.statement: Solar power expected to reduce processing cost by 25-27% (power component); captive solar power at 30-35% of grid cost; solar project IRR 27-28%
items.quote: Overall processing cost, roughly 25% of that, 25% to 27% of that is power. So solar really strategically also from a cost perspective suits us. At the same time, it aligns ourselves with the sustainability targets that we have benchmarked internally for ourselves.

items.statement: Demand strong with latent demand; company operating at optimal capacity utilization for 3.5 months; second half typically heavier due to festive and wedding season
items.quote: Last year was an exception. Last year was an exception. It is usually the other way around. It is the second half, which is heavy.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix: cashew processing 73.70%, commodities trading 26.30%; H1 FY26 and FY26 full year 100% cashew processing, no trading
items.quote: FY '26 we do not have any trading business. What Devyani reported was comparison between first half of FY '25 and first half of FY '26. In '26, we do not have any trading volumes.

items.statement: Phase 2: CNSL oil processing; Phase 3: conversion of CNSL and de-oiled cake into high-value products like cardanol and activated carbon; subsidiary Aelea Green Energy formed for sustainability certification and energy business
items.quote: Phase 2 development of cashew nuts and liquids CNSL means oil processing now in advanced preparatory stages with construction expected to resume post -mortem. Phase 3 conversion of CNSL and real cake into high value products such as cardinal and activated carbon.

items.statement: Cashew prices on downward trajectory for 12 months; pace of decline slowed; corrected roughly 17-18% in last 12 months; consumption growing 6-7% annually
items.quote: On a ballpark basis, it has corrected by roughly 17% to 18%.

items.statement: RCN sourcing: direct from African countries and Indian MNCs at ports; maintain 80-90 days inventory; continuous buying and selling; back-to-back hedging with 3-day price risk
items.quote: We run with a significant inventory which is almost 80-90 days of our total requirements and as and when we keep getting orders, typically we keep selling it and on a daily basis we keep buying it.

items.statement: Input-output ratio: 100 kg RCN yields ~23 kg edible cashew, ~14.4 kg CNSL oil (22% of shell), balance de-oiled cake and charcoal; shells and skin currently sold as scrap
items.quote: The general thumb rule is that you will have roughly 100 kgs of raw cashew nuts going in. You will have 70 kgs of cashew shell and 30 kgs of cashew with the skin. Of that skin will be 7 kgs and typically you will get 23 kgs as your edible cashew. From the 70 kgs of the shell that you have got, typically the oil would be around 22%, which is 14.4 kgs from a raw cashew nuts equivalent.

items.statement: Large volume buyers prefer single supplier for standardized quality and quantity; company maintains healthy net rate and may expand capacity if rate grows significantly
items.quote: A large volume buyer would love to have one single supplier, which can give him a bulk quantity. And that advantage gives us a preferential access to our customers.

items.statement: ~2,000 processors in India; 95% under 10 tons/day capacity; Aelea's 140 tons/day with automation and mechanization is unique in Western India; global advantage vs Vietnam/Africa due to latest tech and integrated value chain vision
items.quote: 95 % of them would be less than 10 tons per day capacity. Their mechanization levels are not up to the levels that we have. Their ability to buy and scale, get the economies of scale is not up to the levels that we have.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced by INR 12 crores vs March 2025; reduction driven by supplier trust enabling working capital efficiency more than interest savings
items.quote: So, yes, borrowings have reduced that is purely from a -- rather than only borrowing from a financial interest perspective, it is actually a very long commitment and trust that our supplier shows in us.

items.statement: Export share expected to increase; sustainability certification via Aelea Green Energy enables premium pricing in European markets where carbon credits traded
items.quote: The sustainability certification part of it really adds to a premium to this oil and biochar, especially from the export market perspective where the certification helps us extra ct a better price from the European market where carbon credits are traded and everything

items.statement: Cashew consumption growing 6-7% annually; price decline beneficial for consumption growth in price-sensitive markets like India
items.quote: From a demand supply perspective, for the next 12 months I can say that there is a significant crop that has been added in the last 1.5 years, 2 years into the market. And that would keep the pressure on the prices to rise from here. Now, that is in a way good from a consumption perspective because whatever replacement can happen of cashew will never happen.

items.statement: Capex spend of ~INR800 crore by end of FY26; total project capex INR6,100-6,200 crore
items.quote: So the present spent of INR200 crores as on 30th September would reach ~ INR800 crores by the end of the fiscal.

items.statement: Total capex for 12 GW cell and 6 GW module is INR6,100-6,200 crore; funded 70% debt, 30% equity/internal accruals
items.quote: the overall spending would be about INR6,100 crores, INR6,200 crores backed by a combination of equity money which came in, debt from lenders and a part of internal accruals as well.

items.statement: Effective capacity utilization 84% in Q2 FY26 and 87% in H1 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter and the half-year-ended 30th September, the effective capacity utilization stood at 84% and 87% respectively.

items.statement: Order book mix: 52% IPP, 20% C&I, 13% distribution, 8% government, 7% EPC; C&I up from 4% to 20% YoY
items.quote: On the customer-wise split, 52% comes from IPPs, 20% from the C&I projects, 13% from the distribution business, 8% from government projects and the balance 7% from EPC. Notably, the C&I segment has witnessed a remarkable surge, now forming 20% of our order book compared to just 4% last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 21.1% in Q2 FY26 (up from 12.6% YoY); PAT margin 11.58% (up from 1.29% YoY); H1 EBITDA margin 21.27%
items.quote: EBITDA at INR235 crores, up by 3x year-on-year basis and margins improving from 12.59% to 21.1%. PAT also showed robust growth, rising 16x year-on-year to INR129 crores with margins at 11.58% as against 1.29% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Module prices fell 4-5% QoQ but costs fell similarly, keeping EBITDA margins flat at ~21%; cell cost ~40% of total cost, BORM ~45%
items.quote: Q1 vis-à-vis Q2, yes, the prices have seen a fall of approx 4% to 5%. Similarly, the costs also have come down. And so you could see that the EBITDA margin for both these quarters are almost at same level

items.statement: Most MSAs have cell cost and tax pass-through; BORM not fully pass-through; no instances of incomplete pass-through
items.quote: The BORM is at times not a pass-through entirely. That is something you need to absorb if there is any increase or additional levy. Or else, the cost on account of cell, the taxes is claimable under the MSAs.

items.statement: India added ~11 GW solar in Q2 FY26; total installed 127 GW as of 30 Sep 2025; ~50% non-fossil capacity
items.quote: As a country, India added approximately 11 gigawatt of solar capacity during the quarter and has reached 127 gigawatt on 30th September. Approximately 50% of India's power capacity today is non-fossil fuel-based.

items.statement: Strong demand from C&I, distribution, PM-KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar; green hydrogen (40-50 GW) and data centre demand emerging; no demand slowdown seen
items.quote: There is a green hydrogen and green ammonia-led of 40-50 gigawatt of additional solar demand that will come in. There is a data centre-led demand that will come in, which will blow up the C&I portion and will not show up in your tendering process.

items.statement: 640 WP G12R module enlisted in ALMM list; first in India; N-type TOPCon cell lines with upgrade provision
items.quote: During the quarter, our latest 640 WP G12R module was enlisted in the recent ALMM list, making us the first company in the country to achieve this milestone.

items.statement: Finance cost H1 FY26 INR60-65 crore vs FY25 INR150+ crore; term loan INR88 crore prepaid in Sep 2025
items.quote: For the year as a whole, FY25, the finance cost was at about 150 plus. And the current H1, with the same impact with increasing volumes, the finance cost is about INR60-INR65 crores for the H1.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from A to A+ in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, I am pleased to share that during the quarter, our credit rating was upgraded from A to A+, reflecting the company's steady financial performance, strong liquidity profile and a prudent leverage management.

items.statement: No full-year guidance provided due to long-term nature of transformer manufacturing
items.quote: To give any sort of guidance as of today will be not right. We would certainly give certain guidance as and when the facility becomes operational at optimum level.

items.statement: Order book at Rs. 1,584 crores as of June 2025 with strong execution visibility
items.quote: Our consolidated order book stands at Rs. 1,584 crores as of 30th June, with strong execution visibility over the few coming months.

items.statement: Order book growing steadily post-June 2025
items.quote: We are seeing a steady growth in the order book. It might not be fair on our part to share as on date numbers, but we can assure you that we are moving at a steady and good pace on the order book side.

items.statement: Order book mix: 17% ≤66 kV, 23% 132 kV, 60% 220 kV
items.quote: Regarding order book, kV class wise up to 66 kV, we have around 17% of the orders; 132 kV, 23% of the orders and 220 kV orders are at 60% of the total orders.

items.statement: Order book customer mix: 70% PSUs, 30% private
items.quote: Typically, the ratio historically also and maybe in a time to come also would be around 70% to 30%, 70% being utility and 30% being the private players.

items.statement: Lead times: 400/765 kV = 18-24 months, 220 kV = 9-12 months, 132/66 kV = 4-6 months
items.quote: The order book build-up in our industry happens kV class-wise. 400 kV class and 765 kV class, typically, it is 18 months to two years of lead time. In 220 kV class, it's about 9 months to 12 months. In 132 and 66, it ranges from four to six months.

items.statement: Input cost pass-through to utilities via transparent pricing formula
items.quote: The 70% business which comes from utility is backed up by the price variation formula. Within any, let's say, variation in the price, we are able to pass it on to the customer on a transparent basis.

items.statement: Demand for 400/765 kV transformers high; state utilities require fewer units than PGCIL
items.quote: Typically, we see a range of about 7 to 10 transformers in a developing state and say about 10 to 15 transformers from a power developed state on yearly basis that comes from each state. Jainam: Got it. Got i t. Those are

items.statement: BTW facility (15,000 MVA) expected to contribute Rs. 600-700 crores revenue in FY26
items.quote: As of today, if we can put 15,000 MVA manufacturing capacity, the total revenue that could be mobilized from this facility ranges between Rs. 600 crores to Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Maintains 20% revenue growth guidance for FY26 and expects EBITDA margin around 19% for next two quarters
items.quote: First of all, yes, we are maintaining that guidance of 20%, and you will see increase in revenue coming up from the current working quarter. So I'm maintaining that guidance, number one.

items.statement: Expects defense revenue of INR200+ crore in FY26, exceeding INR500 crore in FY27, and reaching 4-figure crores in FY28
items.quote: When you come to revenue expected, next year, coming year, which is in the current year, I would say, I expect roughly about INR200- plus crores of revenue from defense. Next year, it should exceed INR500 crores. And year next to that, I'm pretty hopeful. I'm not giving any prediction or guidance, but we should reach in 4 figures.

items.statement: High fibre count cable capacity expansion from 1.73 to 19.01 million fkm p.a. commenced, fully operational by June 2026
items.quote: This quarter marks a transformative milestone for HFCL as we begin the planned expansion of high fibre count Cable manufacturing capacity from 1.73 million fkm p.a. to 19.01 million fkm p.a.. items.quote: We have already achieved a capacity of 28 million fibre kilometres per annum. With all our optical fibre and cable plants now running at full capacity utilisation, we are well-positioned to cater to the surge in global demand.

items.quote: Order book: INR 9981 Crores (as of September 30, 2025) vs. INR 10,480 Crores (previous quarter)

items.statement: HTL secured INR101.82 crore order from Indian Army for Tactical Optical Fiber Cable
items.quote: Our subsidiary, HTL Limited, secured a prestigious contract worth ~₹101.82 crore from the Indian Army for the supply of Tactical Optical Fiber Cable and related accessories.

items.statement: Secured ~INR50 crore order for Thermal Weapon Sights, execution underway at Hosur
items.quote: Additionally, HFCL has secured an order of approximately ₹50 crore for Thermal Weapon Sights, with execution already underway at our Hosur facility.

items.statement: Received additional router orders for BharatNet West Bengal circle, participated in two more circles
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have received additional orders for routers under the BharatNet project for the West Bengal Circle. We have participated in two additional circles this quarter.

items.statement: OFC realisation improved from ~INR850 to ~INR950 per fibre km in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Second, the price, of course, of the fiber optic cable realization has improved from previous realization of fiber optic cable in terms of fiber per kilometre, which was roughly about INR850 per kilometre in last quarter, just the last quarter. items.statement: Global OFC demand surging from hyperscalers, data centres, AI workloads; expects strong demand for 3-5 years
items.quote: I just had one figure. United States as a single country, millions of new servers are being put every year, millions. While in India, we are talking about a lakh every year. items.statement: Passive connectivity solutions revenue expected ~INR400 crore in FY26, reaching 4-figure crores in FY27

items.statement: Telecom product revenue split ~80% OFC, ~20% other products; 5G product revenue impacted by chipset supply issue now resolved

items.statement: Entered Tier-1 telcos in Europe and America for OFC supply, providing export stability

items.statement: Divesting 15.19% stake in Nivetti Systems for INR52.51 crore to focus on core telecom and defence

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh government sanctioned 1,000-acre land parcel for defence manufacturing complex
items.quote: A landmark development during this quarter was the sanction of 1000 acre land parcel by the Government of Andhra Pradesh to set up a defence manufacturing complex.

items.statement: Electronic fuzes in final trial stages, testing expected to complete by November 2025

items.statement: Drone detection radar with soft kill option expected to enter production within FY26; lab trials underway, field trials starting shortly
items.quote: In parallel, we are developing a state-of -the-art drone detection radar with a soft kill option, which is expected to enter production within the current financial year. Lab trials are underway, and field trials are set to begin shortly.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 pre-sales Rs 7 billion, up 34% YoY; H1 FY26 pre-sales Rs 14 billion, up 32% YoY
items.quote: We achieved yet another good pre-sales performance of Rs. 7 billion in Q2 of FY'26, representing a year-on-year growth of 34%.

items.statement: Confident of achieving similar pre-sales growth for full FY26

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity at negligible 0.04x despite strong business development investments
items.quote: This has enabled us to maintain our net debt equity at negligible levels of 0.04x despite the strong investments in business development.

items.quote: EBITDA stood strong at Rs. 78 crores in Q2 FY'26, 108% growth over Q2 FY'25 EBITDA of Rs. 37 crores. EBITDA margins stood at 31% up by 8.73% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Co-lending partner margins higher than organic business

items.quote: Primarily it is organic, the things are moving better nowadays. items.statement: Gross NPA 2.92%, Net NPA 0.83%, PCR 91.88% as of Sep 30

items.statement: SMA 1 at 1.15%, SMA 2 at 1.46% of loan book including SMA 0
items.quote: SMA 1 is 1.15% and SMA 2 is 1.46% including zero.

items.statement: Net profit Rs.295 Crore in Q2, up 22.92% YoY

items.statement: Management targets 250 corporates and INR13-15 crore monthly EWA disbursement by March FY26
