items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet, closing the quarter with a net cash position of ₹ 29.4 billion.

items.statement: Dividend payout raised to 26.3% in FY2025 from 25.5%, targeting >30% by FY2030
items.quote: For FY 2025, we raised our dividend payout to 26.3% from 25.5% last year, in line with our goal of crossing 30% dividend payout by FY 2030.

items.statement: Niyant Maru appointed CFO from October 28, 2025 for interim 9-month period, Gandharv Tongia resigned
items.quote: I would also like to take this opportunity to welcome Mr. Niyant Maru, who will join us as the Chief Financial Officer from October 28, 2025, following Gandharv's resignation. He will serve in this role for an interim period of 9 months, until a suitable successor is appointed.

items.statement: No increase in competitive intensity seen; pricing premium vs peers sustained
items.quote: We are not seeing any particular increase in competitive intensity, and that is perhaps visible in the gross margin that we are delivering. Our pricing premium compared to the other players in the industry continues to be as it is.

items.statement: Wires & Cables volume growth in high-teens, revenue growth 21% YoY on high base (28% YoY last year)
items.quote: The Wires & Cables business delivered a 21% YoY revenue growth, supported by high-teen volume expansion during the quarter.

items.statement: FMEG solar products standout performer driven by central/state rooftop incentive schemes
items.quote: The solar products category was once again the standout performer, driven by robust demand under central and state solar rooftop incentive schemes.

items.statement: US export outlook uncertain due to tariff negotiations; ongoing trade talks may resolve by end-November
items.quote: U.S. is a developing situation. So, it will be very difficult for us to comment at this point of time what we can expect perhaps by the end of this quarter, or maybe in the next quarter or so. We don't know what the tariff number will be by next month either. Hopefully, the ongoing trade negotiations get resolved by the end of November.

items.statement: Income tax search matter: CIT(A) allowed appeals in full, NIL tax demand; order effect pending
items.quote: During the quarter ended 30th September 2025, the CIT(A) allowed the Company's appeals in full, resulting in NIL tax demand. The order giving effect to the CIT(A) decision is currently pending before the assessing officer.

items.statement: HVDC cables not pursued currently; limited domestic projects, no local manufacturing capability, imports used
items.quote: As of now, there are very limited projects in the country that requires HVDC cables. None of the players in the country have the tech to manufacture them, and whatever cables are being utilized or will be supplied for those projects will be imported.

items.statement: Special purpose cables (defense, auto, railway coaches) in low single digits but fastest-growing vertical; demand ~2.5-3% of sector capex
items.quote: You can apply a percentage of about 2.5% to 3% to the capex, which are currently getting committed in these sectors, and that would represent the demand for cables generated from those sectors.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 EBITDA guidance of INR 5,500-6,000 crores
items.quote: All-in-all, ladies and gentlemen, we reaffirm our FY '26 EBITDA guidance in the range of INR 5,500 crores and INR 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR ~47,000 crores (~24 GW) as of September 30, 2025
items.quote: Our order book continues to be strong at INR ~47,000 crores as of September 30, 2025.

items.statement: Total module capacity reached ~18.7 GW (India ~16.1 GW, US 2.6 GW); cell capacity fully operational at 5.4 GW
items.quote: Our total module capacity has touched ~18.7 gigawatts, and our cell capacity is now fully functional and operational at 5.4 gigawatts, the largest cell manufacturing facility of its kind in India.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR ~8,175 crores capex; total capex plan INR 25,000+ crores over next 24 months, back-end loaded
items.quote: Our overall capex program continues with additional INR ~8,175 crores approved by our Board of Directors.

items.statement: Target module capacity 26.7 GW by FY26; cell capacity 15.4 GW and ingot/wafer 10 GW by 2027
items.quote: We intend to operationalize the remaining module capacity expansion in FY '26 to take it to 26.7 gigawatts. Further, by 2027, we intend to scale up our cell capacity to 15.4 gigawatts and ingots and wafer facility of 10 gigawatts by 2027.

items.statement: BESS capacity being scaled from 3.5 GWh to 20 GWh with INR ~8,000 crores investment; first phase 3.5 GWh commercial production expected FY27
items.quote: We are augmenting our battery energy storage system capacity from 3.5 gigawatts hour to 20 gigawatts hours.

items.statement: Acquired 76% stake in Racemosa Energy India (smart meters), 64% in Kotsons (transformers), and Meyer Burger US solar assets
items.quote: We have also made three strategic acquisitions. Smart meters are going to be extremely important components of renewable value chain and hence we have announced 76% stake in Racemosa Energy India. We have acquired 64% stake in Kotsons Private Limited, which marks our entry into the world of transformers. And recently, we have acquired solar manufacturing assets of M eyer Burger in the US, further

items.statement: India solar capacity projected to more than double from ~127 GW to ~280 GW by 2030; US solar to reach ~500 GW by 2030; data center demand to surge from 33 GW to 176 GW by 2035
items.quote: India's solar capacity is projected to move more than double from ~127 gigawatts to around 280 gigawatts by 2030.

items.statement: ALMM extended for cells from June 2026 and ingots/wafers from June 2028; GST cut from 12% to 5% expected to improve affordability
items.quote: The regulatory environment continues to be conducive with initiatives like extension of ALMM for cells since June 2026 and for ingots and wafers from June 2028, aiming further strengthening India's domestic value chain from ingots to modules and reduce rel iance on

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded to 25.17% from 17% YoY; DCR segment carries 300-350 bps higher margin than non-DCR
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also expanded to 25.17 % versus 17% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: US module realizations 26-30 cents/watt vs India non-DCR 16-17 cents/watt; tariff costs passed to customers via change-of-law clauses or negotiation
items.quote: So, the US, typically we have about anything between 28–30 cents. That is the range which is ongoing.

items.statement: Inventory spike to INR ~1,300 crores (vs normal INR 300-400 crores) due to goods-in-transit for export orders; will normalize next quarter
items.quote: This is finished goods. But this time, there's a bump up to almost INR 1300 crores. So, you see that will taper out.

items.statement: Domestic sales mix ~19-20% retail, rest large institutional; retail growing and not fully captured in order book
items.quote: About 19 % to 20% is retail and the rest is large institutional customers, roughly.

items.statement: Order book split ~60% overseas, 40% domestic; Q2 revenue split 53% domestic, 47% overseas; US IRA benefits INR 1.6B in quarter
items.quote: We already spoke about order book and it stands roughly at 24 gigawatts, of which approximately 60% is overseas and balance 40% is domestic.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR 2 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to mention that the Board has approved an interim dividend of INR 2 per share, reaffirming our commitment towards rewarding our shareholders.

items.statement: US AD/CVD investigation ongoing; early days, cooperating fully; supply chain configured to avoid FEOC entities and minimize tariffs
items.quote: I can -- what I can say is that I definitely confirm that the probe is on. Now, it's early days for the probe. So, we really don't know in which direction and what manner will it proceed.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly module production 2.64 GW; cell production 0.6 GW ramping up in H2
items.quote: We have recorded the highest ever quarterly production of 2.64 gigawatts.

items.statement: Expanding into BESS (20 GWh), inverters (4 GW), electrolyser (1 GW), green hydrogen (2027), transformers, smart meters; signed 413 MW PPAs, secured 6.1 GW connectivity
items.quote: We are augmenting our battery energy storage system capacity from 3.5 gigawatts hour to 20 gigawatts hours. The electrolyser manufacturing capacity is being augmented to 1 gigawatt and the inverter manufacturing facility from 3 gigawatts to 4 gigawatts.

items.statement: Partnership with IIT Bombay to train 3,000+ individuals in perovskite and advanced solar cell technologies
items.quote: Our partnership with IIT Bombay will train over 3 ,000 individuals in deep technology and advanced solar cell technologies, particularly the perovskite technology.

items.statement: Completed divestment of 88.2 lakh Indosolar shares via OFS generating INR 523 crores profit classified as other equity
items.quote: Waaree Energies has completed its divestment of about 88.2 lakh equity shares of Indosolar through OFS, and this has generated a profit of about INR 523 crores, and this has been classified as other equity in the consolidated balance sheet.

items.statement: Managing gross margins by back-to-back sourcing; input costs trend with prices with small lag; US supply chain configured to avoid entity-of-concern sources
items.quote: We are always managing Waaree at the gross margin level, because the input cost, as you know, also trends in the direction of the prices.

items.statement: INR 25,000+ crore capex plan excludes acquisitions like Kotsons, Racemosa, Meyer Burger; these are over and above
items.quote: In terms of whether our INR 25,000+ crores capex includes these, the answer to that is no. That is over and above.

items.statement: Ingot-wafer and cell capacity expanded from 6 GW to 10 GW each; projects on schedule for 2027 completion
items.quote: You must have seen that we have actually upped our capacity from 6 gigawatts to 10 gigawatts for ingots and wafers as well as for cells. And so, those projects are moving right on schedule and on time for cells 2027 and for ingots and wafers 2027 completion.

items.statement: Module utilisation 80-85%, cell utilisation 85-90% of nameplate capacity as thumb rule
items.quote: So, like a thumb rule for that, for modules, it is going to be in the region of 80% to 85%. And for cells, it will be, say, 85% to 90%. Thumb rule.

items.statement: Chikhli cell facility to reach 80-85% utilisation within current quarter after key event
items.quote: So, we were waiting for a very important event where the capacity would jump and that event has happened. So, we will make sure that now the amount of production jumps quite dramatically. And yes, within this quarter, we will see that it kind of gets to 80%, 85% utilization pretty quick.

items.statement: Indosolar facility utilisation currently 75%; ramp-up via training, retention, equipment tuning, power stability
items.quote: Utilization of the facility is in the region of around 75%.

items.statement: US facility fully booked; sourcing cells globally meeting FEOC requirements; manufacturing panels for US from both India and US
items.quote: From an overall supply chain, we source cells from all across the world for the US facility, which first of all pass the test of US law. So, there are FEOC requirements, which we need to take care of. So, supply chain is aligned in that manner, number one. And number two, we do send, so I don't know if I made it very clear, but we do manufacture panels for the US from India as well as from the US.

items.statement: Target blended EBITDA margin 22-25% post backward integration; module alone 18-19%, cell adds 300-350 bps
items.quote: The margin should bump up between 300 to 350 basis points overall on a sustained basis. And, of course, you can play with a mix of exports and retail, etc. So, anything between 22% to 25% is a good margin to look at on the backward integration. And that's what we really want to maintain at around like 24%, 25%.

items.statement: North Star EBITDA target INR 5,500-6,000 crores; margin managed to this target regardless of geography
items.quote: The way we manage it is we manage it to our North Star of EBITDA, INR 5,500 crores to INR 6,000 crores. And that's how we would like to deal with it.

items.statement: DCR and non-DCR module margins expected to remain in similar range; pricing may decline slightly with efficiency gains
items.quote: I think it might go down a little bit as manufacturers get better and better in their efficiencies and their own costs kind of go down. But from a margin perspective, I think we will continue to be in a similar range as what we are at this point in time.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar market growing from 3 GW last year to 10 GW this year, more next year; targeting 25-30% market share
items.quote: Last year, it was 3 gigawatts. This year, 10 gigawatts. Next year, probably much more than that. And so, our attempt is to capture a fairly large element of that. Now, I don't want to put an exact number to it, but it would be safe to say that I would like to be somewhere between 25% and 30% of the market share for that.

items.statement: US CBP anti-dumping probe on cells just begun; internal review suggests limited liabilities but outcome uncertain
items.quote: So, that probe by CBP has just begun. And so, it'll be incorrect for us to really comment on potential likely outcomes. Our internal review suggests that we may not be facing a whole host of liabilities as far as that is concerned. But it's best that we wait and understand as the ADD investigation goes ahead.

items.statement: Inverter manufacturing beyond assembly - proper electronic manufacturing with clean rooms; not mere assembly
items.quote: Your question on what level of manufacturing we will be getting into, it is going to be well beyond assembly. You know, we are actually having proper electronic manufacturing equipment, again, clean rooms that are required for doing that. So it is not mere assembly. It is actually a proper assembly of components and related manufacturing.

items.statement: Already in HJT technology via Meyer Burger US facility; production lines flexible for new technologies; actively investing in R&D
items.quote: We actually already are in HJT. We have actually supplied several of these HJT modules. The Meyer Burger facility that we have actually acquired in the U.S. is an HJT facility. So, we are already there as far as that is concerned. But our production line is fairly flexible to take different kinds of technologies, as well.

items.statement: Meyer Burger acquisition (INR 18M) includes manufacturing facility and reasonable cell inventory; cell line not acquired (INR 11M was for inventory only)
items.quote: So, Deepak, I think the number that you mentioned for Waaree, like around INR18 million that you have paid it for, it includes the entire manufacturing facility, right, as well as the some good amount of inventories of cells as well. So ours does not only include the only the manufacturing facility, but along with it, the reasonable amount of quantity of cells as well.

items.statement: Subsidiaries like Indosolar may be consolidated over time; currently focusing on ramping capacity and optimizing operations
items.quote: For any organization which is growing at the pace at which we are growing, we will have subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries which get created. And over a period of time, we might actually think of consolidating some of them as well. At this point in time, predicting how it is going to be would not be a good thing to do.

items.statement: Other expenses rose to 9% from normal 6-6.5% due to higher export mix (freight and duties); expected to normalize
items.quote: So, basically, the other expense also consists of freight and duties, and we have a good mix of our exports this time. So, that has come into play. Normally, you will see when there is a normal spread in terms of the segment, it ranges about 6% and 6.5%. And so, now, this quarter, it is 9%. But of course, we eventually expect it to come down.

items.statement: Substantial cash on balance sheet; forecasted earnings plus undrawn bank borrowings to fund capex; financial closures done ahead of spend
items.quote: As far as the overall support on the capex side, you see a substantial amount of cash lying in the balance sheet even today. And then the earnings that we have forecasted should add up to that to be able to do the entire capex. Also, as you know, that our balance sheet discloses few borrowings that we have taken from the bank, but the drawdown has not happened.

items.statement: Material revenue from new verticals (BESS, inverters, transformers) from FY28 onwards; progressive quarterly commissioning benefits before that
items.quote: So, the actual benefit if you ask me on the announced capex is the last leg of capex is getting completed in FY28. So, FY28 on wards you will see the complete benefit of the announced capex so far. But certainly, quarter on quarter you will see the previous capex getting closed out and benefit start coming in the financial statements.

items.statement: PLI not baked into plans; treated as cherry on top; current performance without PLI
items.quote: We typically don't bake in PLI in our overall plans. It's going to be a cherry on the top as we move forward.

items.statement: Top three risks monitored: cybersecurity, ESG, regulatory environment changes
items.quote: You know, we have all seen what has happened to Jaguar Land Rover. And so, cybersecurity tends to be one of the very important discussions that we have internally to ensure that it is taken care of. ESG and the various elements that go with it is the second risk that we track. And the third risk is the regulatory environment changes that are required -- I mean, that happen all around us and have a

items.statement: BESS technology evolving similar to solar; line configured for lithium-ion but adaptable to sodium-ion; energy density key pacing item
items.quote: From a technology perspective, Nirali, it's very, very similar to solar. It's a continuously evo lving technology. The key pacing item as far as battery technology is concerned is the energy density. How much energy can you pack in a given volume? And that keeps getting better and better and better

items.statement: BESS financial metrics expected similar to Waaree Energies; payback 3-5 years; ROCE/ROE ranges maintained
items.quote: In general, our paybacks are always in between three years to five years range . So, whatever capex that we do on the manufacturing front, we believe this should be no different than what it is today. So, you may continue to see the similar range of ROC E and ROE that you see over a period of time at Waaree Energies level

items.statement: Acquired businesses (Kotsons, Racemosa, Meyer Burger) have Waaree as big internal customer; immediate synergies and alignment
items.quote: I think these are all adjacencies. So from a business perspective, all of these businesses have a big customer. That is the big internal Waaree as a customer. And that's where synergies immediately play out. And that's where the alignment also immediately plays out.

items.statement: Indosolar ramp-up dependent on training, talent retention, equipment fine-tuning, and grid power stability in Noida
items.quote: Our capacity is in the region of – I mean, capacity utilization is in the region of around 70% to 75%. And typically, the way you ramp up is, number one, as your people get more and more trained and understand how to manufacture, it goes up. So, training is a very important component of that. Retention of talent is a very important component of that.

items.statement: Vision to be energy transition major of choice across solar, BESS, hydrogen, transformers, smart meters, inverters
items.quote: From a vision perspective, it's very clear. We want to be the energy transition major of choice , r ight? So, whatever technology, whatever components, whatever ideas are required for energy transition, we should be there and we should be the supplier or vendor of choice

items.statement: PAT target doubled from FY24 Rs 411 cr to Rs 800+ cr by FY27; already at Rs 369 cr in H1 FY26, on track to achieve in 2 years instead of 3
items.quote: We have earlier guided that our ambition was to dou ble our PAT from FY24, which was Rs. 411 crores by FY27. Today, with our progress in just 2 years, we are already nearing this milestone, well ahead of plan

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in FY27 once capacity additions contribute
items.quote: Yes. Definitely, we see double-digit growth.

items.statement: Speciality carbon black brownfield expansion to 130,000 MT by end Q3 FY26, total carbon black capacity 250,000 MT
items.quote: In speciality carbon black, the brownfield expansion project is progressing well, set to more than double our capacity to 130,000 MT per annum by the end of Q3 FY26, Positioning Himadri as the world's largest single-site producer of speciality carbon black, this expansion will take our total carbon black capacity to 250,000 MT per annum.

items.statement: Anthraquinone and carbazole facility expected commissioning by Q2 FY27
items.quote: In parallel, our new speciality chemical segment is gaining momentum with the upcoming facility of anthraquinone and carbazole production that is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY27.

items.statement: LFP cathode active material 40,000 MT plant on track for Q3 FY27 operations; phase capacity 200,000 MT
items.quote: Targeting a phase capacity of 200,000 MT per annum, the in itial 40,000 MT per annum plant is already under development and on track to commence operations by Q3

items.statement: Coal tar pitch distillation capacity increasing from 500,000 MT to 600,000 MT
items.quote: Our current capacity is 500,000 MT. We are going to become 600,000 MT.

items.statement: Birla Tyres PCR plant installation to commence within next 12 months
items.quote: For the passenger car radial unit designed for EVs and SUVs, the installation of plant and machinery is scheduled to co mmence within the next 12 months

items.statement: Speciality carbon black expansion to more than double capacity to 130,000 MT by end Q3 FY26
items.quote: In speciality carbon black, the brownfield expansion project is progressing well, set to more than double our capacity to 130,000 MT per annum by the end of Q3 FY26

items.statement: Coal tar pitch capacity increasing from 500,000 MT to 600,000 MT; utilization impact from Q3, full from Q4/Q1
items.quote: Our current capacity is 500,000 MT. We are going to become 600,000 MT. Sanjesh Jain: How should we think this utilization? Anurag Choudhary: This utilization from Q4, it will start. Q3 will have some impact and Q4 and then from Q1

items.statement: Birla Tyres expects 30-40% capacity utilization next year from current 10%
items.quote: Currently suppose we are running at 10% capacity utilization, next year we expect at least 30% to 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA Rs 243 cr up 21% YoY, PAT Rs 187 cr up 39% YoY; H1 EBITDA Rs 477 cr up 23%, PAT Rs 369 cr up 43%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at Rs. 243 crores, a growth of 21% year-on-year, over Rs. 201 crores in Q2 FY25. PAT stood at Rs. 187 crores, reflecting a 39% increase year-on-year compared to Rs. 134 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven 65-70% by high value-added product mix, 30% by operational efficiency
items.quote: High value-added products contributed around 65 %-70% and 30% was in account of operational efficiency.

items.statement: Margins sustainable, not dependent on raw material price movements; 100% pass-through mechanism
items.quote: 100%. Whether price goes up or down, what difference it will make is only in terms of percentage of margin and in terms of top line. Not in terms of absolute margin

items.statement: Raw material price correction 13-15% YoY impacted revenue; 100% pass-through to customers
items.quote: Corresponding quarter last year, the average raw material price was 13% higher than current prices, 13% to 15%. So, when the prices came down, the realization also came down. That resulted in lower turnover.

items.statement: Volumes at peak capacity utilization; demand strong, no softness; volume growth from Q4 with new capacity
items.quote: The volumes are at the same level basically because we are more or less at peak capacity utilizations. With the new capacity being added in next quarter for speciality ca rbon black and de-bottling neck for the coal tar pitch also happening, then we can see volume growth from Q4 onwards

items.statement: Global demand strong across 54 countries; no significant positivity or negativity
items.quote: See, for us, demand has been strong only. Reason being that our volumes of carbon black are fully sold. So, we do not see any significant positivity or negativity in the demand side earlier also and even today.

items.statement: Over 60 new speciality carbon black grades launched
items.quote: With over 60 new grades launched, we are strengthening our leadership and product diversity in this critical segment.

items.statement: LFP cathode material supplied to IBC for Prabal 2000 cells; encouraging feedback from demo plant
items.quote: IBC is a clear example. So, IBC is coming out with a cell Prabal 2000 with LFP cathode material. For which we sent them the sample, and they tested the material. And they were so pleased to see the quality of the material that we had detailed discussion, and interactions.

items.statement: Achieved ISCC-Plus certification for Mahistikry plant; CDP Supplier Engagement 'A' rating; EcoVadis Platinum (top 1% globally)
items.quote: This quarter, Himadri achieved the ISCC-Plus certification for our Mah istikry plant, reaffirming our dedication to responsible manufacturing and circular economy principles. We earned an ‘A’ rating in CDP's Suppliers Engagement Assessment, reflecting strong supplier collaboration on environmental performance. It's also worth highlighting that we have previously received the prestigious Platinum r

items.statement: Working capital at 31% of topline; expected to remain at same levels for next 3 quarters
items.quote: See, current working capital is 31% of the top line and we expect this to remain in the same levels

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increase due to commercial papers issued against bank deposits; no leveraging
items.quote: So, actually these are commercial papers we have issued against which we have done deposits with banks. So, there is no leveraging we are doing.

items.statement: Strategic investments: Sicona Battery Technologies 17.6%, International Battery Company 16.2%, Invati Creations 40%
items.quote: our strategic investment in Si cona 17.6%, International Battery Company 16.2% and In vati Creations 40% give us access to cutting -edge technologies, R&D capabilities and a presence across the entire LIB value chain for anode and cathode materials to cell manufacturing

items.statement: EBITDA per kg carbon black improved from Rs 15 to Rs 17 over last year
items.quote: We have increased in last one year, the EBITDA per kg from Rs. 15 rupees to Rs. 17.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 8-10% annually for FY26 and FY27 before new capacity comes online
items.quote: We should continue for the next two years to grow in a range of around 8% to 10% every year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 1-2% over next 24 months before new projects start
items.quote: we should be able to further enhance our EBITDA margins ranging around 1% to 2% in next 24 months before the other project starts coming in.

items.statement: Total capex of Rs 1,900-2,000 crore planned through March 2028 across all projects
items.quote: So the total is 900 plus. T hat is somewhere around Rs. 1,900 to Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX happening in March '28

items.statement: Greenfield glass plant in Madhya Pradesh capex of Rs 700 crore, operational by March 2027
items.quote: the overall capital expenditure in terms of land and building and other expenses is odd Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Aluminum beverage can plant phase 1 capex of Rs 850 crore, commercial production by Q3 FY28
items.quote: The total outlay in the first phase is around Rs. 850 crores. A major chunk will be spent by that time, or by December 2027.

items.statement: Debottlenecking and other expansion capex of Rs 120-150 crore in next one year excluding major projects
items.quote: The overall spend in the next one year, I think, on a rollin g basis excluding Gwalior plant or Aluminum beverage CAN, should be in range of odd Rs. 120 crores to Rs. 150 crores

items.statement: North India greenfield glass plant adding 500 TPD (25% increase) to reach 2,600 TPD total by March 2027
items.quote: The project is on track to be operational by March 2027 and will add 500 TPD of new capacity — a 25% increase in our overall glass production — taking our total to 2,600 TPD.

items.statement: Aluminum beverage can plant in UP with 950 million cans annual capacity initially, scaling to 1.6 billion by FY30
items.quote: The facility will be developed in two phases, starting with an annual capacity of 950 million CANS and scaling up to 1.6 billion CANS by FY30.

items.statement: Container glass debottlenecking from 1,850 to 1,900 TPD and specialty glass from 154 to 200 TPD by March 2026
items.quote: Our Container Glass capacity will increase from 1,850 TPD to 1,900 TPD, while our Specialty Glass capacity will see a significant expansion from 154 TPD to 200 TPD

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin at 24.9%, up 250 bps sequentially from adjusted Q1 margin of 22.4%
items.quote: Our Q2 EBITDA margin (excluding other income) was a healthy 24.9%. This represents a significant 250 basis point jump compared to the adjusted Q1 margin of 22.4%

items.statement: Specialty glass EBITDA margin expansion potential of 4-5% over next 18 months
items.quote: for the EBITDA margin expansion, you can easily consider maybe 4% to 5% over the next 18 months happening on the specialty glass.

items.statement: Term loan prepayment of Rs 193 crore in July 2025 reduced term borrowings to Rs 233 crore as of September 2025
items.quote: We have demonstrated our commitment to financial prudence by completing a term loan prepayment of ₹193 crore in July 2025. This has substantially reduced our term loan borrowings to just ₹233 crore as of September 2025

items.statement: Peak debt expected at Rs 1,000-1,200 crore by March 2028 even without equity issuance
items.quote: Rs. 1,000 to 1,200 crores around that.

items.statement: Board approved equity raise resolution, seeking shareholder approval, may execute in next 3-6 months
items.quote: The board passed a resolution to raise equity through various instruments. And we are in process of seeking shareholder approval also and I think it is already up with the shareholders.

items.statement: Current assets holding days increased ~15 days as of Sept 2025, expected to normalize in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: There has been a temporary increase in our current assets holding days by around 15 days as on 30th September 2025 as compared to corresponding last year's figures. These current assets holding levels will normalize during next 1-2 quarters

items.statement: Inventory build-up for Q3-Q4 seasonal demand; receivables delay due to customer software issue, resolved post-quarter
items.quote: the inventory is on account of our continuity of the production, because the upcoming season of 3rd Quarter and 4th Quarter. So we stock the finished goods to be ready when the seasonal market demand in Q3 & Q4.

items.statement: Prices linked to major raw material inputs with time lags of weeks to up to one year depending on contracts
items.quote: we are having an understanding with our customers, with our buyers, that these prices will be linked to the input prices of the major raw material. So, whatever is good, yes , there can be a time lag.

items.statement: Currently using over 40% cullet (recycled glass), expect percentage to increase further with municipal corporation improvements
items.quote: Yes, we are using more than 40% of the cullet. And we will be using more also in the times to come.

items.statement: Current export share 5-7% of revenue; aspiration to reach 10-15% overall and 40% in specialty glass
items.quote: As on today, our export percentage falls anywhere between 5% to 7%. We have an aspiration of increasing our export to 10% to 15%, total. In a specialty glass, this percentage is quite high. And we have an aspiration of taking this percentage to 40% in the s pecialty glass
